name: Product landed cost worksheet
summary: After an import shipment lands, the owner or bookkeeper gets one worksheet: freight, duty, brokerage, insurance and inbound fees from the invoices spread over each product by a stated method, the landed unit cost beside the cost the store records, and the margin left. A person updates any cost.

sources.title: Fully Powered AI's own design: set export headers that stop on a mismatch; units received checked against units invoiced; exchange rates used only as supplied; five charge types with a stop on any line that fits none; duty taken product by product from the customs entry as entered, counted once when the broker passes it on, with every customs question recorded for the broker and left unanswered; an allocation method per charge type; shares rounded to the cent with the remainder on the largest basis and a rounding check against the shipment total; the store's recorded cost as the comparison, with a percentage flag; margins at the recorded cost and the cost to enter against a floor; a new version for a late invoice; and a draft cost update list with the line for the books and a blank approval line.

sources.contribution: Counting the cost of bringing a shipment in as part of each unit's cost before it sells; a proportional share of those charges by each product's part of the shipment's value, divided by its units; keeping a sales tax the business recovers out of cost; the warning that a missing cost reads as full margin in store reports; and weighted average as one way to hold a running cost.

Never placing a shipment's charges a second time; shares in proportion rather than equal parts; each product's share turned into a cost per unit; and actual cost set against an expected cost, marked above or below and ordered from the biggest gap down.
The reminder that a shipment's charges come on bills of their own, sometimes long after the stock is on the shelf.
Sharing a shipment's charges by weight, volume or units as well as by value.
